contest:D1.note: accepted; the documentation is then taken down and the sponsor contests: the acceptance is in doubt until the developer brings the document back and a round reads it again, and then it is paid

contest:D2.note: accepted; the documentation is then taken down, the sponsor contests, and it never comes back: still in doubt when the window ends, it is rejected

contest:Q2.note: second in the queue and satisfies every requirement: the sponsor contests, the reading is upheld, and once the first can no longer be accepted it is paid the whole reward

contest:R1.note: the service runs, the documentation never says how a client authenticates: rejected on the judged requirement, contested by the developer, rejected again

create:cancelled_funded.note: funded, then given up before any submission

create:cancelled_unfunded.note: given up before it was funded

create:doubt_lost.note: an acceptance put in doubt and never restored

create:doubt_restored.note: an acceptance put in doubt and restored

create:queue.note: three submissions, the second is paid

create:returned.note: five submissions, none accepted: the reward goes back

evaluate:D1.note: accepted; the documentation is then taken down and the sponsor contests: the acceptance is in doubt until the developer brings the document back and a round reads it again, and then it is paid

evaluate:D2.note: accepted; the documentation is then taken down, the sponsor contests, and it never comes back: still in doubt when the window ends, it is rejected

evaluate:Q1.note: first in the queue with a service that is not there yet: it is read late and rejected, and until its time has run out nobody behind it is paid

evaluate:Q2.note: second in the queue and satisfies every requirement: the sponsor contests, the reading is upheld, and once the first can no longer be accepted it is paid the whole reward

evaluate:Q3.note: third in the queue and also satisfies every requirement: an earlier submission is paid first, and this one gets its bond back

evaluate:R1.note: the service runs, the documentation never says how a client authenticates: rejected on the judged requirement, contested by the developer, rejected again

evaluate:R2.note: good documentation of a service whose status answer does not report the routes: the check that calls it is not met

evaluate:R3.note: the documentation addresses the evaluator: the judged requirement is not met without the panel, and the checks are still decided in code

evaluate:R5.note: a service that is not there: the round decides nothing, and when the read-by time passes the submission lapses

final:D1.note: accepted; the documentation is then taken down and the sponsor contests: the acceptance is in doubt until the developer brings the document back and a round reads it again, and then it is paid

final:D2.note: accepted; the documentation is then taken down, the sponsor contests, and it never comes back: still in doubt when the window ends, it is rejected

final:Q1.note: first in the queue with a service that is not there yet: it is read late and rejected, and until its time has run out nobody behind it is paid

final:Q2.note: second in the queue and satisfies every requirement: the sponsor contests, the reading is upheld, and once the first can no longer be accepted it is paid the whole reward

final:Q3.note: third in the queue and also satisfies every requirement: an earlier submission is paid first, and this one gets its bond back

final:R1.note: the service runs, the documentation never says how a client authenticates: rejected on the judged requirement, contested by the developer, rejected again

final:R2.note: good documentation of a service whose status answer does not report the routes: the check that calls it is not met

final:R3.note: the documentation addresses the evaluator: the judged requirement is not met without the panel, and the checks are still decided in code

final:R4.note: a deliverable nobody asks to have evaluated: when its read-by time passes it lapses, and its bond goes to the sponsor

final:R5.note: a service that is not there: the round decides nothing, and when the read-by time passes the submission lapses

outage:down.note: the branch no longer serves either document

outage:restored.note: the branch serves the first document again
